facts.statement: Thaisaurus was an extinct marine reptile that lived during the Spathian stage of the Early Triassic.
facts.quote: Thaisaurus is an extinct genus of ichthyopterygian marine reptile that lived during the Spathian (late Olenekian, Early Triassic).

facts.statement: Fossils of Thaisaurus have been found in Thailand.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found in Thailand.

facts.statement: The type specimen was discovered by Chongpan Chonglakmani on Khao Thong hill near Phattalung, Thailand.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Thaisaurus was discovered by Chongpan Chonglakmani on the hill Khao Thong, around Phattalung, Thailand.

facts.statement: The type specimen is housed in the Department of Mineral Resources in Bangkok with the catalog number TF2454.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed in the Department of Mineral Resources of Bangkok, where it received the number TF2454.

facts.statement: Mazin and colleagues named the species Thaisaurus chonglakmanii in 1991 to honor Thailand and its discoverer.
facts.quote: Mazin and colleagues described the specimen in 1991, naming it Thaisaurus chonglakmanii, in honor of the country it came from and its discoverer.

facts.statement: Thaisaurus was a small ichthyopterygian, a type of marine reptile.
facts.quote: Thaisaurus is a small ichthyopterygian, a group of marine reptiles.

facts.statement: Thaisaurus shares similarities with Chaohusaurus but also exhibits distinct anatomical differences.
facts.quote: While rather similar to its fellow ichthyopterygian Chaohusaurus, Thaisaurus also shows some differences.

facts.statement: Thaisaurus possessed a skull with enlarged, rounded eye sockets and a long, thin snout.
facts.quote: The skull of Thaisaurus bears enlarged, rounded orbits (openings that housed the eyes) and is drawn out into a long, thin snout.

facts.statement: Thaisaurus had narrow, pointed teeth of identical shape firmly set in extensive, partially enclosed sockets.
facts.quote: The narrow, pointed teeth of Thaisaurus are all identical in shape and firmly implanted in extensive, partially enclosed sockets.

facts.statement: The vertebrae in front of the hips of Thaisaurus were short, contrasting with the much longer vertebrae in its tail.
facts.quote: The centra (bodies) of presacral vertebrae, those in front of the hips, are short measured from front to back, differing from the much more elongate vertebrae in the tail.

facts.statement: Thaisaurus had forelimbs that were longer than its hindlimbs, both made of elongated bones.
facts.quote: The forelimbs of Thaisaurus are longer than its hindlimbs, with both sets of limbs composed of elongated bones.

facts.statement: Maisch established the monotypic family Thaisauridae for Thaisaurus in 2010.
facts.quote: In 2010, named a new monotypic family, Thaisauridae, for the former.

facts.statement: Motani argued in 2003 that some features considered unique to Thaisaurus were actually misinterpretations of the fossil.
facts.quote: In 2003, however, Motani argued that some of these supposed distinctive features were actually a result of misinterpretation on the fossils.

facts.statement: Thaisaurus was an extinct genus of ichthyopterygians that lived in the Early Triassic of what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Thaisaurus es un género extinto de ictiopterigios que vivió en el Triásico inferior de lo que ahora es Asia.

facts.statement: Thaisaurus is classified within the family Thaisauridae.
The genus Thaisaurus was established by Mazin and colleagues in 1991.

rejected.statement: Motani suggested in 2003 that the Thaisaurus specimen might represent a juvenile Chaohusaurus, pending further preparation.
rejected.quote: He considered it possible that the specimen instead represented a juvenile Chaohusaurus, though noted that more preparation would be needed before more detailed study could be conducted.

rejected.statement: Motani classified Thaisaurus as Ichthyopterygia incertae sedis in 1999 due to poor preservation preventing detailed analysis.
rejected.quote: Due to its poor preservation, Motani did not include Thaisaurus in the analysis, instead listing it as Ichthyopterygia incertae sedis.

rejected.statement: Maisch and Matzke found in 2000 that Thaisaurus was the first-diverging member of the ichthyopterygian group.
rejected.quote: Maisch and Matzke in 2000... included Thaisaurus in their analysis, finding it to be the first-diverging member of the group.

rejected.statement: The parent group of the genus Thaisaurus is the family Thaisauridae.
